backlogged.summary: `harness learn --hub <empty> --json --compare <v1> <v2>` prints the plain-text "no field data" line instead of the JSON structure (`{since, projects: 0, events: 0, versions: [], candidates: [], message: "no field data"}`) that docs/SPEC.md's general prose says --json produces for the no-data case; lib/commands/learn.mjs's `opts.json && !opts.compare` guard special-cases --compare out of the JSON branch. Not covered by any frozen criterion's check (ES-1's loop never combines --json with --compare) and ES-1's literal text ('출력하고 exit 0') is still satisfied, so this doesn't block, but it's a real doc/behavior gap worth a backlog note.

F59's own test suite (test/f59-learn.test.mjs) is thorough, but resume-safety of the new per-feature build-total aggregation (lib/run.mjs addBuildTotals, e.build) across a process restart (`harness run --resume`) isn't directly exercised — only a single in-process two-round run is tested. Reading the surrounding code, e.build is mutated on the same object held in state.active and persisted by save() after each step, so it appears resume-safe by inspection, but no test pins this.
